cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere. Tip about 10 percent in restaurants; not in pubs.
name: Cardiff
tagline: Wales' capital of castles, rugby and the bay
summary: Cardiff is the lively capital of Wales, with a Roman-Norman-Victorian castle right in the centre. Tour the lavish Gothic rooms of Cardiff Castle, catch a rugby match at the Principality Stadium, explore the redeveloped Cardiff Bay, see the fairy-tale Castell Coch, and walk the open-air St Fagans museum of Welsh life.
seasonNote: Summer is mildest; rugby internationals in February and March fill the city.
arrival: Trains from London Paddington take about 2 hours; Cardiff Airport is 40 minutes away.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; buses and the water bus to the bay.
foodTip: Welsh cakes, Welsh rarebit, cawl (lamb stew) and laverbread.
buyTip: Welsh love spoons and Welsh wool blankets.

items.name: Cardiff Castle
items.summary: Roman walls, a Norman keep and Victorian Gothic rooms of dazzling colour.
items.tip: Take the house tour for the Arab Room.

items.name: National Museum Cardiff
items.summary: Free museum with one of Britain's best Impressionist collections and natural history.
items.tip: See the Davies sisters' Monets and Van Goghs.

items.name: Cardiff Bay
items.summary: Waterfront with the Senedd, Wales Millennium Centre and the Norwegian Church.

items.name: Principality Stadium
items.summary: Wales' national rugby stadium with a retractable roof, in the city centre.
items.expect: Tours paid; match tickets sell fast.

items.name: Castell Coch
items.summary: Red fairy-tale castle in the woods with painted Victorian rooms.
items.tip: Walk in the beech woods around it.

items.name: St Fagans National Museum of History
items.wiki: St Fagans National Museum of History
items.summary: Open-air museum of rebuilt Welsh buildings across 2,000 years.
items.tip: Visit the bakery for fresh bread.

items.name: Victorian arcades
items.summary: Covered arcades of independent shops and cafés.
items.tip: Spillers Records is the world's oldest record shop.

items.name: Welsh cakes
items.summary: Griddle cakes with currants, warm from the bakestone.
items.tip: Buy them warm at the market.

items.name: Cawl and Welsh rarebit
items.summary: Lamb and leek broth, and cheese on toast made the Welsh way with ale and mustard.
items.tip: Try both on a cold day.

items.name: Brains pubs
items.summary: Pubs serving local ales before and after rugby.
items.tip: Go to the Goat Major for pies.

cashTip: Cards are used everywhere; some places are card only.
name: Utrecht
tagline: Two-level canals, the Dom Tower and bikes everywhere
summary: Utrecht is a medieval university city with unusual two-level canals whose old wharf cellars are now cafés at water level. Climb the Dom Tower, the tallest church tower in the Netherlands, visit Miffy's museum and the Rietveld Schröder House, and paddle the canals in a canoe.
seasonNote: Spring and summer for terraces by the water.
arrival: Trains from Amsterdam take about 25 minutes, from Schiphol 30.
gettingAround: Walk or bike; Utrecht has the world's largest bike parking under the station.
foodTip: Wharf-cellar cafés, stroopwafels and Dutch cheese.

items.name: Dom Tower
items.summary: Gothic tower of 465 steps, the tallest church tower in the Netherlands.

items.name: Oudegracht wharves
items.summary: Two-level canal with wharf cellars turned into terraces at water level.

items.name: Rietveld Schröder House
items.summary: UNESCO De Stijl house of sliding walls and primary colours.
items.tip: Combine with the Centraal Museum ticket.

items.name: Miffy Museum
items.summary: Museum for small children about Dick Bruna's Miffy.
items.tip: The Centraal Museum opposite has Bruna's studio.

items.name: Museum Speelklok
items.summary: Museum of music boxes and street organs, demonstrated on guided tours.
items.tip: Join a tour so the organs play.

items.name: Canal canoe or boat
items.summary: Paddle or cruise the Oudegracht under the low bridges.

items.name: Wharf-cellar cafés
items.summary: Cafés and restaurants in the old canal cellars.

items.name: Stroopwafels at the market
items.summary: Fresh syrup waffles pressed at the Vredenburg market stalls.

items.name: Brewery café Ledig Erf
items.summary: Classic Dutch beer café on a canal corner with a huge Belgian beer list.
items.tip: Sit on the terrace by the water.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; service is included in prices.
name: Loire Valley
tagline: Renaissance châteaux and the garden of France
summary: The Loire Valley is France's château country, a gentle river valley of Renaissance palaces, vineyards and gardens. See Chambord's double-helix staircase, Chenonceau spanning the Cher river, Leonardo da Vinci's last home at Clos Lucé in Amboise, and the gardens of Villandry, then taste Vouvray and Chinon wines and cycle the Loire à Vélo route.
seasonNote: May to September; many châteaux hold light shows on summer evenings.
arrival: TGV trains from Paris to Tours or Saint-Pierre-des-Corps take about 1 hour.
gettingAround: A car is easiest; château shuttle buses and bike rental work in summer.
foodTip: Rillettes de Tours, goat cheeses like Sainte-Maure, tarte Tatin and Vouvray and Chinon wines.

items.name: Château de Chambord
items.summary: The biggest Loire château, with a double-helix staircase and 400 rooms.
items.tip: Climb to the roof terraces of chimneys.

items.name: Château de Chenonceau
items.summary: "Ladies' château" built in arches across the Cher river.
items.tip: Go at opening; walk around to see the arches.

items.name: Château d'Amboise
items.summary: Royal château above the river with Leonardo da Vinci's tomb in its chapel.
items.tip: Views from the terraces over the Loire.

items.name: Clos Lucé
items.summary: Manor where Leonardo da Vinci spent his last years, with models of his inventions in the park.

items.name: Villandry gardens
items.summary: Formal Renaissance gardens including a vast ornamental vegetable garden.

items.name: Château d'Azay-le-Rideau
items.summary: Small château rising from a mirror-still moat.

items.name: Loire à Vélo
items.summary: Flat bike route along the river between châteaux and wine villages.
items.expect: Rent bikes in Amboise or Tours.

items.name: Rillettes and goat cheese
items.summary: Rillettes of Tours on bread and Sainte-Maure goat cheese.

items.name: Vouvray wine cellars
items.summary: Caves cut into the tuffeau cliffs pouring Chenin Blanc.

items.name: Tarte Tatin
items.summary: The upside-down caramel apple tart, born in the Loire.
items.tip: Have it warm with crème fraîche.

cashTip: Carry some cash; many small places still prefer it.
name: Füssen
tagline: Neuschwanstein and the castles of King Ludwig
summary: Füssen is the Bavarian town at the end of the Romantic Road, beneath King Ludwig II's fairy-tale Neuschwanstein Castle. Tour Neuschwanstein and the yellow Hohenschwangau, see the castle from Mary's Bridge, swim in the Alpsee, and visit Ludwig's Linderhof palace and the painted village of Oberammergau.
seasonNote: Summer is busy; autumn colours and snowy winters are lovely. Mary's Bridge closes in ice.
arrival: Trains from Munich take about 2 hours; buses run from Füssen station to the castles.
gettingAround: Bus 73 or 78 to Hohenschwangau; walk or horse carriage up to Neuschwanstein.
foodTip: Käsespätzle, roast pork, pretzels and Bavarian beer.
buyTip: Füssen lutes and violins history, and Bavarian crafts.

items.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
items.summary: King Ludwig II's fantasy castle on a crag, the inspiration for Disney's castle.
items.expect: Timed tours; tickets sell out in summer.

items.name: Mary's Bridge (Marienbrücke)
items.summary: Footbridge over a gorge with the classic view of Neuschwanstein.
items.expect: Crowded; closed in snow and ice.

items.name: Hohenschwangau Castle
items.summary: Yellow castle where Ludwig grew up, facing Neuschwanstein.
items.tip: Combine both castles in one ticket.

items.name: Alpsee
items.summary: Clear mountain lake below the castles with a lakeside path.
items.tip: Walk the loop or rent a rowing boat.

items.name: Füssen old town
items.summary: Painted lanes, the High Palace with trompe-l'oeil walls and St. Mang's monastery.

items.name: Linderhof Palace
items.summary: The smallest of Ludwig's palaces, with a grotto and formal gardens.

items.name: Oberammergau
items.summary: Village of painted houses, home of the Passion Play.

items.name: Tegelberg cable car
items.summary: Cable car to a mountain with views over castles and lakes.
items.tip: Walk down the summer luge after.

items.name: Käsespätzle
items.summary: Egg noodles with melted cheese and crispy onions.

items.name: Bavarian Gasthaus
items.summary: Roast pork, dumplings and pretzels in a wood-panelled inn.

items.name: Beer garden by the Lech
items.summary: Outdoor beer gardens with mountain views.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; service is included in prices.
name: Normandy (Bayeux)
tagline: The Bayeux Tapestry and the D-Day beaches
summary: Bayeux is the best base for Normandy: a medieval town that survived the war almost untouched, home to the 70 m Bayeux Tapestry of 1066. From here visit the D-Day landing beaches of Omaha and Juno, the cliffs of Pointe du Hoc, the American Cemetery, Arromanches' Mulberry harbour, and the painters' harbours of Honfleur and the cliffs of Étretat.
seasonNote: June brings D-Day anniversary events (6 June); spring and September are calmer.
arrival: Trains from Paris Saint-Lazare take about 2h20.
gettingAround: A car or a guided D-Day tour; the beaches are spread out.
foodTip: Camembert and Pont-l'Évêque cheese, moules à la crème, cider, Calvados and teurgoule rice pudding.

items.name: Bayeux Tapestry
items.summary: The 11th-century embroidered story of the Norman conquest of England.
items.expect: The tapestry is on loan to the British Museum in London until mid-2027 while the Bayeux museum is rebuilt; check before you go.
items.tip: The audio guide walks you scene by scene.

items.name: Bayeux Cathedral
items.summary: Norman Gothic cathedral where the tapestry was first displayed.

items.name: Omaha Beach and American Cemetery
items.summary: Clifftop cemetery of 9,387 graves above the D-Day beach.
items.tip: Visit the centre first, then walk down to the beach.

items.name: Pointe du Hoc
items.summary: Clifftop battlefield still cratered by bombs, scaled by US Rangers.
items.tip: Walk among the craters and bunkers.

items.name: Arromanches and the Mulberry harbour
items.summary: Remains of the floating harbour built for D-Day, seen from the cliffs.

items.name: Juno Beach Centre
items.summary: Canada's D-Day museum at the beach where Canadians landed.

items.name: Honfleur
items.summary: Painters' harbour of tall slate-fronted houses and a wooden church.
items.tip: Eat moules by the Vieux Bassin.

items.name: Étretat cliffs
items.summary: Chalk arches and a needle rising from the sea, painted by Monet.

items.name: Moules à la crème
items.summary: Mussels in Normandy cream and cider.

items.name: Cheese, cider and Calvados
items.summary: Camembert, Livarot and Pont-l'Évêque with farm cider and apple brandy.
items.tip: Visit a cider farm on the Route du Cidre.

items.name: Teurgoule
items.summary: Cinnamon rice pudding baked for hours.
items.tip: Pair with a glass of pommeau.

cashTip: The local money is the lek (about 100 to the euro); carry cash, as many small places do not take cards. Prices here are shown in euros.
name: Tirana
tagline: Colourful capital of bunkers, cafés and mountains
summary: Tirana is Albania's colourful, fast-changing capital. Walk the huge Skanderbeg Square, go underground in the Bunk'Art bunker museums about the communist era, sip coffee in the trendy Blloku, once closed to all but party leaders, and ride the Dajti cable car up the mountain above the city.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are pleasant; July and August are hot.
arrival: Tirana International Airport is 25 minutes from the centre.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; taxis are cheap; buses to other towns leave from the North-South terminal.
foodTip: Tavë kosi (baked lamb in yogurt), byrek, fërgesë and raki.
buyTip: Raki, olive oil and handmade filigree.

items.name: Skanderbeg Square
items.summary: Vast paved square with the national hero's statue, the Et'hem Bey Mosque and the National History Museum.

items.name: Bunk'Art 2
items.summary: Interior Ministry nuclear bunker turned museum of the communist secret police.
items.tip: Allow time to read; it's sobering.

items.name: Bunk'Art 1
items.summary: Enver Hoxha's giant five-floor bunker, now a museum and gallery.
items.tip: Combine with the Dajti cable car.

items.name: Dajti Express cable car
items.summary: Long cable car to Mount Dajti with views over the city.

items.name: Blloku
items.summary: Former party-elite district, now full of bars, cafés and nightlife.

items.name: Pyramid of Tirana
items.summary: Communist-era pyramid rebuilt as a tech hub you can climb.
items.tip: Climb the steps to the top.

items.name: House of Leaves
items.summary: Museum of secret surveillance in the former secret-police building.

items.name: Tavë kosi
items.summary: Lamb baked under an eggy yogurt crust, Albania's national dish.

items.name: Byrek
items.summary: Flaky pie with cheese, spinach or meat from bakeries.

items.name: Pazari i Ri
items.summary: Restored market square with produce and restaurants around it.
items.tip: Eat in a terrace restaurant around the market.

cashTip: The local money is the lek (about 100 to the euro); carry cash, as many small places do not take cards. Prices here are shown in euros.
name: Berat
tagline: The town of a thousand windows
summary: Berat is a UNESCO Ottoman town of white houses whose many windows stare across the Osum river. Climb to the inhabited castle with its Byzantine churches and the Onufri icon museum, walk the Mangalem and Gorica quarters, and visit the Osumi canyon and wineries nearby.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn; summer is hot.
arrival: Buses from Tirana take about 2.5 hours.
gettingAround: Walk; the castle climb is steep.
foodTip: Slow-cooked lamb, stuffed peppers and local wines from the Berat hills.

items.name: Mangalem quarter
items.summary: Hillside of white Ottoman houses with rows of windows facing the river.
items.tip: View it from the Gorica bridge.

items.name: Berat Castle (Kala)
items.summary: Lived-in castle with Byzantine churches, cobbled lanes and views.
items.tip: Stay for sunset on the walls.

items.name: Onufri Iconographic Museum
items.summary: Icons by the 16th-century master Onufri in the Cathedral of St. Mary.

items.name: Gorica quarter and bridge
items.summary: Quieter quarter across the old stone bridge.

items.name: Ethnographic Museum
items.summary: Ottoman merchant house showing traditional life.

items.name: Osumi Canyon
items.summary: River canyon for rafting in spring and hikes.
items.expect: About 1h30 away; rafting March to May.

items.name: Berat wineries
items.summary: Family wineries pouring local Shesh i Zi and Puls reds.

items.name: Traditional lamb
items.summary: Slow-cooked lamb and stuffed peppers in family restaurants.
items.tip: Ask for the dish of the day.

items.name: Byrek and coffee by the river
items.summary: Morning byrek and strong coffee on the boulevard.
